source: Register of St. George, Hanover Square, 1725-1809 (Harleian Society), i. 284
record_text: 1778. — John Parry and Eliz. Bayless: ibid. i. 284.

meaning: variant (corruption) of Baynham
author_comment: A corruption to which there are many parallels; v. Deadman, Putman, Swetman. This surname is still familiar to co. Wilts, bordering on the district where Baynham arose. There cannot be a doubt as to the origin.
source: Register of Canterbury Cathedral, 1564 onwards (Harleian Society), p. 59
record_text: 1658. Married — Richard Bayman to Hannah Curlinge: Canterbury Cath., p. 59.

meaning: Ab-Eignon (Welsh), i.e. the son of Eignon or Ennion
author_comment: A Gloucestershire surname. Robert ap Eignon had for his son Robert Baynham, of Chorewall, in the forest of Dean. Henceforward the family were so known (vide Visitation of Gloucestershire, 1623, p. 14; Harleian Soc.). The name looks wonderfully English and local, but, as shown, is not so. Beynon, Binyon, and Benyon, q.v., are other forms; but not Bunyan, I think.
source: Visitation of Gloucestershire, 1623 (Harleian Society), p. 13
record_text: Thomas ap Eignon, 7 Edw. III: Visitation of Glouc., 1623, p. 13.
